clue.text: Wild outfit, Albert, for song

parts.note: wild in the sense of furious or crazy, mad
a rig or rig-out is a set of clothes, an outfit
Al is the short form of the name Albert

explanation.surface: Someone called Albert wears an eccentric costume to perform a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several unaccompanied voices, popular in Renaissance Europe.

clue.text: The way of some, tho 'dangerous

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is a part taken from the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A warning that a certain route, though some use it, is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'some', all of 'tho' and the start of 'dangerous'.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a way or manner of doing something.

clue.text: Mended -blast!

explanation.surface: A repair job interrupted by a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Mended socks were repaired with needle and wool; as an exclamation it is a mild oath, a euphemism for damned.

clue.text: Ron is outside in fetters

indicators.note: turning something outside in, like inside out, jumbles its parts, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ron is out of prison, though clapped in chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are shackles or chains, as in a prisoner clapped in irons.

clue.text: Repays for Geneva's reconstruction

indicators.note: reconstruction means building again from the same parts, so the city's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is read as the plain letters of the name followed by S

explanation.surface: Money handed back for rebuilding the Swiss city.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to repay or requite it with retribution.

clue.text: Azed has one in pub at eastern market

indicators.note: in places the setter and the extra letter inside the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub or the room in one where drinks are served
Azed is A-Zed, the letters A and Z spelt out in British style; it is also the name of a famous crossword setter
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: The veteran setter Azed is having a drink in a pub at an Oriental market.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed is the pseudonym of the Observer's long-running crossword setter, but read as 'A Zed' it gives the letters A and Z (Zed being the British name of the last letter).
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a marketplace in the Middle East or Asia, a covered street of stalls.

clue.text: Ella and Violet meeting head-on had a meal to relieve the pain

indicators.note: for two names to meet head to head, the first is turned around so its start touches the second

parts.note: Vi is a familiar short form of the name Violet
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: Two women, Ella and Violet, get together over lunch to ease their sorrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting head-on' means Ella is turned round so that her head (her first letter) faces Violet's short name, as two people meet face to face.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate is to lessen suffering, to ease or soothe it.

clue.text: Haphazardly drunk, new matador

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A newly qualified bullfighter staggers about, drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things at random means without plan or pattern, by chance.

clue.text: Determined and did the crossword again

explanation.surface: A puzzler is set on completing the same grid twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolved means firmly decided; split as re-solved it means worked out once more.

clue.text: Pie — a busy shopkeeper has a big one

definitions.text: a busy shopkeeper has a big one

explanation.surface: A busy shopkeeper sells a lot of pies.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnover is a pastry folded over a filling; it is also the total value of sales a business makes.

clue.text: Torches broad trousers

explanation.surface: Flaming brands and bell-bottoms side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Flares are blazing lights used as signals; they are also trousers widening from the knee down.

clue.text: Let it stand with time in frame

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for a frame

parts.note: a set is a frame or framework, as in a stage set

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave a picture in its frame for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: STET is the proof-reader's mark (Latin for 'let it stand') cancelling a correction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is a Latin instruction to an editor to keep a deleted passage.

clue.text: Supervision is a mistake

explanation.surface: A comment that keeping watch can itself be an error.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversight means watchful management, and also an error made through failing to notice.

clue.text: Meat around the north may be bought

indicators.note: around signals that the meat word wraps the compass letter

parts.note: veal is meat from a calf
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Meat from up north is on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A venal official is corruptible, open to bribery.

clue.text: April 4, December 1, February 2, August 5, March 15

indicators.note: the number beside April picks out that position in the month's name, its fourth letter
the number beside December picks out that position in the month's name, its first letter
the number beside February picks out that position in the month's name, its second letter
the number beside August picks out that position in the month's name, its fifth letter

explanation.surface: A list of dates, as if from a diary.
explanation.walkthrough: The list looks like dates, but each number counts letters into its month: the 4th of April, 1st of December, 2nd of February and 5th of August. The last date is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides fell on the 15th of March, May, July and October, famously the day Caesar was killed.

clue.text: Stop fellow getting cleanser

parts.note: to deter someone is to stop or discourage them
a gent is a fellow, a man

explanation.surface: Preventing a man from obtaining a cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergent is a cleaning agent, such as washing powder.

clue.text: Got up after meal for flower

indicators.note: after puts the getting-up word behind the meal word

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal
rose means got up

explanation.surface: Someone rises from the table and goes off to pick a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a garden rose with a scent said to resemble tea.

clue.text: Type of invoice from university lecturer or master

parts.note: prof is short for professor, a senior university teacher
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Paperwork from an academic or a graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma invoice is a preliminary bill sent in advance of goods.

clue.text: Bird on fire, love

parts.note: flaming means burning, on fire
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A passionate declaration of burning love.
explanation.definitionFit: The flamingo is a tall pink wading bird.

clue.text: Told of broken treadle

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone recounted the tale of a damaged sewing-machine pedal.
explanation.definitionFit: Related here means narrated, as when a story is related or told.

clue.text: Obscure English coin

parts.note: dim means obscure or faint

explanation.surface: An old English coin that few have heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English coin' looks like the definition, but the coin is American: a dime is a ten-cent piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is a US ten-cent piece.

clue.text: Ship's staff from railway junction, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is chosen for how it is spoken

parts.note: Crewe is a town in Cheshire, England, famous as a major railway junction

explanation.surface: Sailors arriving at a station, so we are told.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is the company of people who work a ship.

clue.text: String player in the little room, first

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison
1st, with the figure read as the letter I, abbreviates first

explanation.surface: A violinist practises in a small room before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist plays the cello, a bowed instrument of the violin family.

clue.text: Dog at party upset Warsaw inhabitant outside

indicators.note: outside puts the Warsaw native around the overturned party

parts.note: a Pole is someone from Poland, whose capital is Warsaw

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, turns the word upside down so it reads upwards

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A pet at a party is upset because a Polish guest shuts it out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means the party word reads upwards; the Polish person then sits outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The poodle is a curly-coated breed of dog.

clue.text: Sleeping places on board or docks

explanation.surface: Bunks on a ship and moorings for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Berths are bunks on a ship or train; to berth a ship is to moor it, so it docks.

clue.text: Bone of iron by French wall

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
mur is the French word for wall

explanation.surface: A skeleton part made of metal found next to a wall in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone.

clue.text: Factory gem can be very heavy round one's neck

parts.note: a mill is a factory, such as a cotton mill
a stone is a gem, a precious stone

explanation.surface: A jewel from a factory becomes a burden worn as a necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: A millstone round one's neck is an idiom for a heavy burden or responsibility.

clue.text: Some spurious language

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: A remark that part of what is said is false.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'spurious' and the start of 'language', and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal, unofficial language, which purists might call spurious.

clue.text: Athlete and climber

explanation.surface: A sporting all-rounder who also scales cliffs.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is an athlete who races on foot; it is also a climbing plant such as a runner bean.

clue.text: Trap brigand who's lost his head with drink

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter of the word for a brigand is dropped

parts.note: a bandit is a brigand or robber

explanation.surface: An outlaw is caught after drinking too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and It is a cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin and It is a cocktail of gin with sweet Italian vermouth.

clue.text: Takes over having trouble with pupil teachers

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
PTs are pupil-teachers, senior pupils who once taught younger ones in British schools

explanation.surface: A school with difficult trainee staff is taken over.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea is to take it over as one's own.

clue.text: Gives a shock to totters

explanation.surface: A surprise makes someone reel.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggers means astonishes or amazes, and also walks unsteadily.
